get_account_summary.title: Get the account's IAM summary
get_account_summary.description: Read the account's IAM usage and quotas -- how many users, roles, policies and MFA devices exist, against the limits. The cheapest call that proves the credentials work, and a quick read on account hygiene (`AccountMFAEnabled` on the root user especially).

output.description: The account's IAM entity counts and quotas.

get_account_password_policy.title: Get the account password policy
get_account_password_policy.description: Read the password policy for IAM users -- minimum length, required character classes, rotation and reuse rules.

update_account_password_policy.title: Update the account password policy
update_account_password_policy.description: Change the IAM password policy for the whole account. Tightening it applies to every user's next password change; `HardExpiry` can lock users out when their password expires, so set it deliberately.

require_uppercase.description: Require at least one upper-case letter.

require_lowercase.description: Require at least one lower-case letter.

allow_users_to_change_password.description: Let users change their own passwords.

max_password_age.description: Days before a password must be changed.

password_reuse_prevention.description: How many previous passwords may not be reused (1-24).

hard_expiry.description: Prevent users from changing an expired password themselves -- they then need an administrator, so this can lock people out.

get_account_authorization_details.title: Export the account's IAM configuration
get_account_authorization_details.description: Dump users, groups, roles and policies with their attached and inline policy documents in one call -- the whole permission graph, which is what an access review actually needs. Large on any real account, so page it.

filter.description: Restrict the dump to one entity type.

max_items.description: How many entities to return per page.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

output.description: The account's users, groups, roles and policies with their documents.

generate_credential_report.title: Generate a credential report
generate_credential_report.description: Ask IAM to build the account credential report -- every user's password, key and MFA status. Generation is asynchronous; poll get_credential_report until it is ready.

output.description: The report's state and when it was produced.

get_credential_report.title: Get the credential report
get_credential_report.description: Download the credential report as base64-encoded CSV -- one row per user, with password age, key age, last use and MFA. The standard input to a key-rotation or dormant-account audit.

output.description: The report content, base64-encoded, with its format and generation time.

list_users.title: List IAM users
list_users.description: Read the account's IAM users. `path_prefix` narrows to a path such as "/engineering/", and paging is by `marker` rather than page number.

path_prefix.description: Only users whose path starts with this, e.g. "/engineering/".

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

output.description: The users, with `IsTruncated` and a `Marker` when there are more.

get_user.title: Get an IAM user
get_user.description: Read one user -- their ARN, path, creation date, tags and password last used. Omit `user_name` to read the user the credentials themselves belong to.

user_name.description: The user's name. Omit to read the calling identity.

create_user.title: Create an IAM user
create_user.description: Create an IAM user. They start with no permissions and no credentials -- attaching a policy and creating an access key or login profile are separate, deliberate steps. `permissions_boundary` caps what they can ever be granted.

path.description: IAM path for the user, e.g. "/engineering/". Defaults to "/".

permissions_boundary.description: ARN of a managed policy that caps the user's maximum permissions, whatever else is attached.

update_user.title: Rename or move an IAM user
update_user.description: Change a user's name or path. Renaming keeps the same principal id but **breaks any policy that names the old user ARN**, so search for references first.

delete_user.title: Delete an IAM user
delete_user.description: Delete an IAM user. IAM refuses while they still have access keys, a login profile, MFA devices, inline policies, attached policies or group memberships -- so this is the last step of an offboarding, not the first. Irreversible.

list_user_tags.title: List a user's tags
list_user_tags.description: Read the tags on an IAM user, which policies can condition on.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

tag_user.title: Tag an IAM user
tag_user.description: Add or replace tags on a user. Tags can be load-bearing: policies condition on `aws:PrincipalTag`, so a tag change can grant or remove access.

untag_user.title: Remove a tag from an IAM user
untag_user.description: Remove one tag from a user. If a policy conditions on it, the user loses that access immediately.

list_access_keys.title: List a user's access keys
list_access_keys.description: Read a user's access key ids with their status and creation date -- the list a key-rotation policy is enforced against. Secrets are never returned.

user_name.description: The user's name. Omit for the calling identity.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

get_access_key_last_used.title: Get when an access key was last used
get_access_key_last_used.description: Read when and where an access key was last used -- date, region and service. The evidence for retiring a key nobody admits to owning.

output.description: The key's owner and last-used date, region and service.

create_access_key.title: Create an access key
create_access_key.description: Mint a long-lived access key for a user. **The secret is returned once and never again**, and IAM allows only two keys per user. Prefer roles and short-lived credentials -- a leaked static key is the most common cause of an AWS compromise.

user_name.description: The user to create the key for. Omit for the calling identity.

output.description: The new key id and its secret -- shown only this once.

update_access_key.title: Activate or deactivate an access key
update_access_key.description: Change a key's status. Deactivating is the reversible half of a rotation: the key stops working immediately but can be turned back on, unlike a delete.

user_name.description: The key's owner. Omit for the calling identity.

delete_access_key.title: Delete an access key
delete_access_key.description: Permanently delete an access key. Anything still using it fails at once and it cannot be restored -- deactivate first, wait, then delete.

user_name.description: The key's owner. Omit for the calling identity.

list_mfa_devices.title: List a user's MFA devices
list_mfa_devices.description: Read the MFA devices registered to a user, with their serial numbers.

user_name.description: The user's name. Omit for the calling identity.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

deactivate_mfa_device.title: Deactivate a user's MFA device
deactivate_mfa_device.description: Detach an MFA device from a user. It weakens their account immediately and can break policies that require MFA -- the usual reason to do it is a lost device.

serial_number.description: The device's serial number or ARN, from list_mfa_devices.

get_login_profile.title: Check whether a user has console access
get_login_profile.description: Read a user's login profile -- whether they have a console password at all, and whether it must be reset. A 404 here means API-only access.

user_name.description: The user's name. Omit for the calling identity.

output.description: The login profile, or an error when the user has no console access.

delete_login_profile.title: Remove a user's console access
delete_login_profile.description: Delete a user's console password. They keep any API credentials, so this is half of an offboarding, not all of it.

list_groups.title: List IAM groups
list_groups.description: Read the account's IAM groups, with their paths and ARNs.

path_prefix.description: Only groups whose path starts with this.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

get_group.title: Get a group and its members
get_group.description: Read one group with the users in it -- the membership half of a permission review.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

create_group.title: Create an IAM group
create_group.description: Create a group. Groups carry policies rather than credentials, which makes them the maintainable place to grant a team's permissions.

path.description: IAM path for the group. Defaults to "/".

delete_group.title: Delete an IAM group
delete_group.description: Delete a group. IAM refuses while it still has members or policies, and deleting it removes whatever access it granted them.

add_user_to_group.title: Add a user to a group
add_user_to_group.description: Put a user in a group, granting them every policy the group carries. This is a real permission change and takes effect within seconds.

remove_user_from_group.title: Remove a user from a group
remove_user_from_group.description: Take a user out of a group; they lose the group's policies immediately. Check whether they reach the same permissions another way before assuming access is revoked.

list_roles.title: List IAM roles
list_roles.description: Read the account's roles with their trust policies and paths. Service roles live under paths like "/aws-service-role/", which is how to tell them from your own.

path_prefix.description: Only roles whose path starts with this.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

get_role.title: Get an IAM role
get_role.description: Read one role -- its ARN, trust policy (who may assume it), session duration and tags. The trust policy is the important half.

output.description: The role, including its assume-role policy document.

create_role.title: Create an IAM role
create_role.description: Create a role. `assume_role_policy_document` decides **who may become it** -- a service, an account, a federated identity -- and getting it wrong is how roles end up assumable by the wrong party. Pass the policy as a JSON string.

assume_role_policy_document.description: The trust policy as a JSON string -- who is allowed to assume this role. This is the security boundary.

path.description: IAM path for the role. Defaults to "/".

permissions_boundary.description: ARN of a managed policy capping the role's maximum permissions.

update_assume_role_policy.title: Change who may assume a role
update_assume_role_policy.description: Replace a role's trust policy. This is the single most security-relevant write in IAM: it decides which principals can become the role, and it replaces the document wholesale rather than merging.

policy_document.description: The complete new trust policy, as a JSON string.

delete_role.title: Delete an IAM role
delete_role.description: Delete a role. IAM refuses while it has inline or attached policies or belongs to an instance profile. Anything currently assuming it -- an EC2 instance, a Lambda, a CI pipeline -- loses access at once.

list_role_tags.title: List a role's tags
list_role_tags.description: Read the tags on an IAM role, which policies can condition on.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

tag_role.title: Tag an IAM role
tag_role.description: Add or replace a tag on a role. As with users, policies can condition on role tags, so this may change access.

list_instance_profiles.title: List instance profiles
list_instance_profiles.description: Read the account's instance profiles -- the wrappers through which EC2 instances receive a role.

path_prefix.description: Only profiles whose path starts with this.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

output.description: The instance profiles and the roles inside them.

list_policies.title: List managed policies
list_policies.description: Read managed policies. `scope` of "Local" is your own policies and "AWS" the AWS-managed ones -- default is both, which is thousands of entries, so narrow it. `only_attached` finds the ones actually in use.

scope.description: "Local" for customer-managed, "AWS" for AWS-managed, "All" for both.

only_attached.description: Only policies attached to at least one user, group or role.

path_prefix.description: Only policies whose path starts with this.

policy_usage_filter.description: Whether the policy is used for permissions or as a boundary.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

get_policy.title: Get a managed policy
get_policy.description: Read a managed policy's metadata -- description, default version, and how many entities it is attached to. Use get_policy_version for the document itself.

get_policy_version.title: Get a managed policy's document
get_policy_version.description: Read the actual permission statements of one policy version. The `DefaultVersionId` from get_policy is the version currently in force.

list_policy_versions.title: List a managed policy's versions
list_policy_versions.description: Read a policy's versions and which is the default. IAM keeps at most five, so a create can fail until an old one is deleted.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

create_policy.title: Create a managed policy
create_policy.description: Create a customer-managed policy from a JSON document. Creating it grants nothing until it is attached -- but write it narrowly anyway, since `"Action": "*"` in a policy that later gets attached widely is how accidents happen.

policy_document.description: The policy as a JSON string.

path.description: IAM path for the policy. Defaults to "/".

description.description: What the policy is for. Cannot be changed later.

delete_policy.title: Delete a managed policy
delete_policy.description: Delete a customer-managed policy. IAM refuses while it is attached to anything or has non-default versions, and everything that relied on it loses those permissions.

list_entities_for_policy.title: List what a policy is attached to
list_entities_for_policy.description: Read the users, groups and roles a managed policy is attached to. The call to run before changing or deleting a policy -- it tells you the blast radius.

path_prefix.description: Only entities whose path starts with this.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

output.description: The attached users, groups and roles.

list_attached_user_policies.title: List a user's attached policies
list_attached_user_policies.description: Read the managed policies attached directly to a user. Inline policies are separate -- see list_user_policies -- and group policies are a third source, which is why "what can this user do" needs all three.

path_prefix.description: Only policies whose path starts with this.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

list_attached_role_policies.title: List a role's attached policies
list_attached_role_policies.description: Read the managed policies attached to a role.

path_prefix.description: Only policies whose path starts with this.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

list_attached_group_policies.title: List a group's attached policies
list_attached_group_policies.description: Read the managed policies attached to a group, which every member inherits.

path_prefix.description: Only policies whose path starts with this.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

attach_user_policy.title: Attach a policy to a user
attach_user_policy.description: Grant a user everything a managed policy allows. A real privilege change, effective within seconds -- and attaching an AWS-managed administrator policy makes them an account administrator.

policy_arn.description: ARN of the managed policy to attach.

detach_user_policy.title: Detach a policy from a user
detach_user_policy.description: Remove a managed policy from a user. They may still hold the same permissions through a group or an inline policy, so verify with simulate_principal_policy rather than assuming.

policy_arn.description: ARN of the policy to detach.

attach_role_policy.title: Attach a policy to a role
attach_role_policy.description: Grant a role everything a managed policy allows. Every workload assuming the role gains those permissions on its next session.

policy_arn.description: ARN of the managed policy to attach.

detach_role_policy.title: Detach a policy from a role
detach_role_policy.description: Remove a managed policy from a role. Live workloads lose those permissions, so expect immediate failures if the policy was in use.

policy_arn.description: ARN of the policy to detach.

attach_group_policy.title: Attach a policy to a group
attach_group_policy.description: Grant every member of a group what a managed policy allows -- the widest of the three attach calls, since it applies to everyone in the group at once.

policy_arn.description: ARN of the managed policy to attach.

detach_group_policy.title: Detach a policy from a group
detach_group_policy.description: Remove a managed policy from a group; every member loses those permissions.

policy_arn.description: ARN of the policy to detach.

list_user_policies.title: List a user's inline policies
list_user_policies.description: Read the names of policies embedded directly in a user. Inline policies are invisible to list_attached_user_policies, which is why permissions audits miss them.

max_items.description: How many policy names to return.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

get_user_policy.title: Get a user's inline policy
get_user_policy.description: Read the document of one inline policy on a user.

put_user_policy.title: Set an inline policy on a user
put_user_policy.description: Embed a policy directly in a user, replacing any policy of the same name. A direct privilege grant that no managed-policy audit will show -- prefer attaching a managed policy where you can.

policy_name.description: A name for the inline policy. Reusing one replaces it.

policy_document.description: The policy as a JSON string.

delete_user_policy.title: Delete a user's inline policy
delete_user_policy.description: Remove an inline policy from a user; they lose those permissions immediately.

list_role_policies.title: List a role's inline policies
list_role_policies.description: Read the names of policies embedded directly in a role.

max_items.description: How many policy names to return.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

get_role_policy.title: Get a role's inline policy
get_role_policy.description: Read the document of one inline policy on a role.

put_role_policy.title: Set an inline policy on a role
put_role_policy.description: Embed a policy directly in a role, replacing any policy of the same name. Every workload assuming the role gains it -- a real privilege grant.

policy_name.description: A name for the inline policy. Reusing one replaces it.

policy_document.description: The policy as a JSON string.

delete_role_policy.title: Delete a role's inline policy
delete_role_policy.description: Remove an inline policy from a role. Anything assuming the role loses those permissions.

simulate_principal_policy.title: Test what a principal is allowed to do
simulate_principal_policy.description: Ask IAM whether a user or role would be allowed to perform given actions on given resources, evaluating every policy that applies. The right way to verify a permission change -- it answers with allowed or denied and names the statement responsible, without touching anything.

policy_source_arn.description: ARN of the user, group or role whose permissions to evaluate.

resource_arn.description: The resource ARN to test against. Defaults to "*".

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

output.description: Per-action decisions -- allowed or denied -- with the matched statements behind each.

simulate_custom_policy.title: Test a policy document before using it
simulate_custom_policy.description: Evaluate a policy you have written, without attaching it to anything. The safe way to check that a new policy allows what you intend and nothing more.

policy_document.description: The policy to evaluate, as a JSON string.

resource_arn.description: The resource ARN to test against. Defaults to "*".

output.description: Per-action decisions with the matched statements.

generate_service_last_accessed_details.title: Start a service last-accessed report
generate_service_last_accessed_details.description: Ask IAM to work out which services a user, role or policy has actually used, and when. Asynchronous -- it returns a job id that get_service_last_accessed_details polls. The evidence base for cutting unused permissions.

arn.description: ARN of the user, role, group or policy to analyse.

granularity.description: Whether to report at service or action level.

get_service_last_accessed_details.title: Get a service last-accessed report
get_service_last_accessed_details.description: Read the result of a last-accessed job -- which services were used and when, or never used at all. Poll until its status is COMPLETED.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

output.description: The job's status and the per-service last-accessed data.

list_saml_providers.title: List SAML identity providers
list_saml_providers.description: Read the SAML providers configured in the account -- the trust anchors for federated console and CLI access.

list_openid_connect_providers.title: List OIDC identity providers
list_openid_connect_providers.description: Read the OpenID Connect providers in the account -- what makes GitHub Actions or a Kubernetes service account able to assume a role without static keys.

list_virtual_mfa_devices.title: List virtual MFA devices
list_virtual_mfa_devices.description: Read the account's virtual MFA devices and which user each is assigned to. `Unassigned` devices are leftovers worth cleaning up.

assignment_status.description: Only devices in this assignment state.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

list_server_certificates.title: List server certificates
list_server_certificates.description: Read the IAM-stored server certificates with their expiry dates -- the legacy store still used by some ELB and CloudFront configurations.

path_prefix.description: Only certificates whose path starts with this.

marker.description: Paging marker from a previous response.

output.description: The server certificates and their expiry dates.
